title: Completed matching comparison on principal opens from the punctured isomorphism
statement: Let A be a commutative local ring with maximal ideal m, C its m-adic completion, U an open subset of Spec A, q:Y→U any scheme morphism and s:E→Spec C a finite morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Let D be completion overlap data, with its actual matching ring B and punctured comparison Y→(Spec B)×_Spec(A)U [def-sbc-punctured-completion-matching-sections]. Assume this punctured comparison is an isomorphism. Let P=B pushout_A C, psi:P→Gamma(E) the completed matching comparison [def-sbc-completed-matching-ring-map], and j:A→P the structural map through B. For any f in A such that D(f) is contained in U, the induced map P localized away from j(f)→Gamma(E) localized away from psi(j(f)) [def-weil-ring-localization-away] is bijective. No Noetherianity, punctured-spectrum condition on U, or finiteness of q is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0BLH (completion overlap) and 05ER (proposition-equivalence, second paragraph, localized comparison); the geometric base-change assembly from an assumed punctured comparison is written and proved by G4.

proof.text: By naturality of the Spec–Gamma unit and the ring-pullback condition, the two maps from the overlap to Spec B obtained via Y and via E agree. Transport the pullback of q and the restricted completion map along D.overlapIso and the assumed isomorphism D.puncturedMap. Paste the restriction square of Spec B→Spec A. This gives the pullback square with source the completed inverse image of U and projections to Spec B and the completed inverse image of U in Spec C.

Put P=B pushout_A C and k=E.toSpecGamma≫Spec.map(completedRingMap). The two defining pushout equations and unit naturality show that k followed by the Spec B projection is D.fromCompleted, and k followed by the Spec C projection is s. Mathlib isPullback_SpecMap_pushout gives the corresponding pullback square for Spec P. Restrict this square over the completed inverse image of U. Pullback cancellation (IsPullback.of_right) compares it with the square in step 1; its other horizontal arrow is an identity. Hence the restricted k is an isomorphism.

Since s is finite over the affine Spec C, E is affine and E.toSpecGamma is an isomorphism. Cancel its restriction from the restricted k to obtain an isomorphism for Spec.map(completedRingMap) over the inverse image of U in Spec P. The pushout condition identifies the preimage of D(f) through the Spec C route with the basic open of j(f) through the Spec B route. Containment D(f)≤U therefore lets us restrict this isomorphism further to D(j(f)); restriction twice is identified with one restriction by morphismRestrictRestrict.

Use Mathlib SpecMapRestrictBasicOpenIso to identify this restricted Spec map with Spec.map of Localization.awayMap of the original ring map at j(f). Apply isIso_SpecMap_iff to obtain the required bijection. These are canonical constructions and work also for empty principal opens and zero localization rings.

lean.statement:
theorem completedRingMap_away_bijective_of_puncturedMap_isIso
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    {U : (Spec (.of A)).Opens}
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} {q : Y ⟶ U.toScheme}
    {E : Scheme.{u}} {s : E ⟶ Spec
      (.of (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A))} [IsFinite s]
    (D : CompletionGluingData A U q E s) [IsIso D.puncturedMap]
    (f : A) (hf : (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f : (Spec (.of A)).Opens) ≤ U) :
    Function.Bijective (Localization.awayMap D.completedRingMap.hom
      ((D.baseMap ≫ pushout.inl _ _).hom f))
